_readme: THE OWNER'S OWN 30th Celebration MASTER SET. This is the only page on the
site that tracks what he personally owns rather than what he has pulled on
camera, and the two are different: data/hits.json is a record of hits that
appeared in a video, and this is a record of cards in a binder however they
got there -- pulled, traded, or bought as a single.
HOW IT GETS FILLED IN. He lists the cards after a 30th video and they get
added here by hand, one object per card. There is no form, no login and no
browser storage anywhere in this feature, and that is deliberate: the site
is static files, so a localStorage tracker would live in one browser on one
device, would be lost the first time he cleared site data, and would be
invisible to search engines and to him on his phone. A committed JSON file
renders into the page at build time, works everywhere, survives a new
laptop, and is in git history.
FIELDS
name     the card, as printed. Required.
n        collector number, when known. OPTIONAL and often absent,
because the English numbering was not published before release;
a card with no number still counts and still draws a pocket.
section  one of: pikachu, main, secret, classic, energy. Required, since
it decides which binder page the card lands on.
got      the date it entered the binder, YYYY-MM-DD.
video    the YouTube id it was opened in, when it was opened on camera.
Absent for a trade, a single, or a card from before the tracker.
note     anything worth saying. Optional.
DUPLICATES ARE NOT RECORDED HERE. A master set is one of each; a second
copy changes nothing on this page. If doubles ever need tracking that is a
different file, not a count on these objects.
THE DENOMINATOR IS NOT OFFICIAL AND THE PAGE SAYS SO. TPCi has never
published a card count for this set -- checked against its product showcase
and both press releases. PokeBeach counts 199 in English and that is the
number the progress bars run against, attributed to them every place it is
shown. It may move when the last secret rares are revealed. See
data/30th.json's readme.
SO 0 OF 199 IS THE CORRECT STARTING STATE, not a bug. The set releases 16
September 2026 and this file was written on the 11th.
REBUILT FROM TYPED NUMBERS, 21 September 2026, AND THAT IS NOW THE WAY IN.
The owner: "I will actually go back through and just send over the card numbers for
each card, that way you dont have to read the image, and can just match the card
image up with the card number". Everything before this was identified off
photographs -- by HP and attack name for the Pikachu, because their numbers were
not legible at that angle -- and a typed number is his own reading of the card
where that was mine. The list he sent is the whole binder, so this REPLACES rather
than merges; `got`, `shot`, `illus` and the identification notes were carried
forward for every card that was already on file, and the 45 new ones carry no date
because none was given and inventing one would be the same class of error this
rebuild exists to remove.

owned.name: Basic Grass Energy
owned.note: The owner, 16 September 2026, photographing them laid out. READ STRAIGHT OFF THE CARD, which is possible here and was not for the rotated Pikachu photograph: each one prints "MEE EN" and its number in the footer, large enough to read, alongside YOSHIROTTEN's name. THE MEE SET CODE IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THESE ROWS: the eight foil basic Energy are numbered in a DIFFERENT set from the 128 Pokemon and Trainers, which is why no /128 appears on them and why TCGplayer lists none of them under either 30th Celebration set name. data/30th-checklist.json holds zero Energy rows, so these eight can only ever be entered by hand from a card in front of him, The picture comes from `pid`: TCGplayer files all eight under its own "MEE: Mega Evolution Energies" set, not under either 30th Celebration name, which is why they were missed. This one reads MEE EN 009.

THIS IS THE ONE NUMBER IN THE PHOTOGRAPH I AM INFERRING RATHER THAN READING, and it is recorded as such. Its footer is the least legible of the eight. Six others in the same photograph read cleanly -- Grass 009, Fire 010, Water 011, Lightning 012, Darkness 015, Metal 016 -- and those six sit in the standard Pokemon energy order (Grass, Fire, Water, Lightning, Psychic, Fighting, Darkness, Metal) with no gaps except 013 and 014. Psychic is fifth in that order, so it is 013 and Fighting is 014. Six confirmed readings pinning a sequence is a strong inference, but it is still an inference: if a Fighting Energy ever turns up reading 013, this row is the one to check first.

owned.name: Pikachu
owned.note: The owner, 16 September 2026: "here are all the pikachu cards i pulled today", with a photograph of nine laid out. IDENTIFIED BY HP AND ATTACK NAME, NOT BY READING THE COLLECTOR NUMBER: the photograph is rotated a quarter turn and the numbers sit small and angled at the card edge, where a misread digit puts the wrong card in the binder. The HP and the attack line are large and legible, and across all 30 of this set's Pikachu every one of these attack names appears EXACTLY ONCE -- checked against TCGplayer's own card text for the whole subset before any of these were written. So the identification is a lookup rather than a reading. This one is HP 60, [LC] Pika Ball (20), with the Lonely Gaze Ability above it, which is #028 and nothing else. No `shot`: he asked for sourced scans rather than his own photographs, so the pocket draws the checklist's picture.

So the identification is a lookup rather than a reading. This one is HP 70, [C] Play Rough (10+), which is #047 and nothing else. No `shot`: he asked for sourced scans rather than his own photographs, so the pocket draws the checklist's picture. A DOUBLE WAS RECORDED AGAINST THIS CARD ON 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 AND IT WAS WRONG. The first photograph was rotated a quarter turn and I read two cards in it as Play Rough; asked whether that was a double or a misread, he answered double, and it went in here. A clearer, upright photograph the same day shows exactly ONE Play Rough -- this card, 047/128, subset 25/30 -- and the repeated card is a second Get Some Air, 046/128. The claim is removed rather than moved, because a second copy is not recorded anywhere in this file by design. THE LESSON IS IN THE QUESTION, NOT THE ANSWER: he was asked "double or misread?" without being told that #052 Angry Bolt is also HP 70 with a (10+) attack, which is the fact that makes two cards easy to confuse. A question that hides the discriminating detail gets a confident answer to the wrong question, and his answer was reasonable given what he was told.

owned.name: Fuecoco ex
owned.note: The owner, 16 September 2026: "regular double black star - double rare", with a close-up. This set prints Fuecoco ex twice, 015/128 Double Rare and 147/128 Special Illustration Rare, and the two carry IDENTICAL text -- HP 210, Singe, Cheerful Flame (70x) -- so only the rarity mark and the artwork separate them. Two black stars IS the Double rare symbol, and the close-up shows 015/128 with the 30C set code, so the symbol and the printed number agree. That agreement is the check: either alone would have been enough to act on, and having both means nothing here rests on my reading of a small number in a photograph.

owned.name: Hydreigon
owned.note: Read off the card: 099/128, set code 30C, regulation mark J, Stage 2 evolving from Zweilous, 170 HP. NOT in Japan's 176 card list at all, which is the clearest single proof that the English set is a different set and not a translation of it.

owned.name: Jirachi ex
owned.note: The owner, 16 September 2026: "Jirachi ex is the double black star - double rare". THE SYMBOL IS THE ANSWER AND THE TEXT COULD NEVER HAVE BEEN: this set prints Jirachi ex twice, 102/128 Double Rare and 155/128 Special Illustration Rare, and the two carry IDENTICAL card text -- HP 160, Wish Granter, Swift (150) -- so nothing readable separates them. Only the rarity mark and the artwork do. Two black stars IS the Double rare symbol, which is the same rule the rip log rows on this site follow, so this is 102. IT WAS WORTH ASKING RATHER THAN GUESSING: 102 is $5.63 raw and 155 is $580.00, so a coin flip here would have been wrong by a hundredfold while looking exactly as confident as being right.

owned.name: Eevee
owned.note: The owner, 16 September 2026: "these were the hits from the packs I ripped today", with a photograph of ten. IDENTIFIED BY CARD TEXT, NOT BY READING THE COLLECTOR NUMBER, for the reason the Pikachu rows record: a number read off a photograph is a digit away from putting the wrong card in the binder. THREE EEVEE SHARE THIS SET AND THE TEXT SEPARATES THEM CLEANLY: 116, 117 and 118 are all Common and all HP 70, but 117 and 118 both attack with Quick Attack (20+) and only 116 reads [C] Fetch and Hide followed by [C] Tackle (10), which is what the card in the photograph says. So this is a lookup on the attack line and not a guess between three lookalikes. No `shot`: sourced scans are preferred over his own photographs. SET CODE ADDED 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 for the same reason the Classic Collection rows got theirs: this was the one remaining pocket rendering a bare "#116" with no set marker, which is exactly the ambiguity the owner objected to. Every owned pocket now names its code, and the three codes in this file mean three real things -- 30C is the set, MEE is the Energy sheet the eight foil basics are numbered in, MEP is a promo that is not part of the 199.

owned.name: Igglybuff
owned.note: Read off the card: 120/128, set code 30C, regulation mark J, 30 HP. Japan prints this card too, at #096, so the same card sits at two different numbers in the two sets. That is the numbering mismatch this page keeps warning about, demonstrated on one card.

owned.name: Poke Pad
owned.note: The Trainer in the same photograph, and the only one of the ten cards there that the checklist can confirm outright: it holds Poke Pad at 126/128 Common, and the card reads 126/128 with the 30C set code. Yuko Morii illustrated it. Printed "Poke Pad" here without the accent to match the checklist's own spelling, which is what the renderers key on.

owned.name: N
owned.note: The owner, 17 September 2026, sending its TCGplayer link outright after I could not identify it from the photograph. Product 716202 is N, 101/101, Classic Collection. THE NAME IS THE REASON THE LOOKUP FAILED AND IT WOULD NEVER HAVE WORKED. Every other card in that batch was found by reading its name or its card text and looking it up; this one is named "N", a single character, on a full-art textured Supporter where the nameplate is the hardest part of the card to read. There was nothing to search for. It was sitting in data/30th-checklist.json the whole time -- it appeared in the very first Classic Collection pull as "101/101 N | id 716202" -- and no amount of re-reading the photograph would have got there, which is worth recording as the limit of the identify-by-text method rather than as a near miss. A 30th Celebration card in the Classic Collection, carrying its original set's 101/101 rather than an /128 number. Unique at 101 in that section, unlike the two cards numbered 11 and the three numbered 106. The owner, 17 September 2026: "this is from the 30th Celebration set though, the 30th Celebration set is reprinting some of the most iconic cards in the series so to mark it for the correct set would be to mark it for the 30th Celebration Set". He is right and the card proves it: TCGplayer reports setCode 30C for every card in the Classic Collection, the SAME code as the 128 main set, checked across both set names on 17 September. So these are 30th Celebration cards that carry an INHERITED NUMBER, not visitors from another set. THE POCKETS WERE MISLEADING BEFORE THIS. Sneasel rendered as "#25/111" and Erika's Jigglypuff as "#69/132" with no set marker at all, so the only thing a reader saw was another set's numbering; N had 30C only because it was added later. All three now carry it and every classic pocket reads "#<number> 30C". THE ENERGY IS THE ONLY REAL OUTLIER IN THIS FILE: those eight print MEE, a genuinely different set code, which is why they are the one section whose cards nobody lists.

_shotNote: EVERY `shot` IS THE OWNER'S OWN PHOTOGRAPH of the card in his hand, built by
scripts/build-30th-cards.py from a master in assets-source/30th-cards/.
The value is the master's stem; the builder resolves the renditions.
A card with no `shot` falls back to a TCGdex scan, and if TCGdex has no set
yet it draws as a pocket with no picture. See that script's header for why
photographs rather than scans: on 11 September 2026 no scan of this set
existed in any source this site may use.
_promoNote: PROMOS ARE TRACKED AND ARE NOT PART OF THE 199. This is the whole reason they
live in their own key instead of a sixth section in `owned`: the five sections
add to 199 because that is what the set is -- 128 main, 33 secret, 30 Classic
Collection, 8 Energy -- and a promo is in none of them. Dropping one into a
section would count it toward the denominator and quietly make the percentage
on the page wrong, which is the one number the owner asked to see.
THEY ARE STILL WORTH TRACKING AND HE ASKED FOR THEM. TPCi cut the Nidorina and
Ditto illustration rares from the English set and turned them into product
promos, and there is a Mew at MEP105, so this is a real run alongside the set
rather than a stray card. The set code on the card is the tell: a set card
reads 30C or MEE, a promo reads MEP.
NO DENOMINATOR HERE, DELIBERATELY. Nobody has published how many 30th promos
there will be, and this file does not invent counts -- the same rule that
keeps 199 attributed to PokeBeach everywhere it appears. The page shows how
many he holds and does not imply how many exist.

_jumboNote: JUMBO CARDS ARE TRACKED AND ARE NOT PART OF THE 199, for exactly the reason the
promos are not: the five sections add to 199 because that is what the SET is,
and an oversized card is in none of them. A jumbo in a section would count
toward the denominator and quietly make the completion percentage wrong, which
is the one number the owner asked this page to show.
THEY ARE ALSO NOT THE SAME THING AS THE PROMOS and get their own key rather
than sharing one. A jumbo is a PHYSICAL FORMAT -- an oversized card that does
not fit a nine pocket page and is not tournament legal -- while a Black Star
Promo is a distribution channel. The same artwork can exist as both, which is
precisely why they cannot share a list: the owner's Greninja ex exists here as a
standard-size promo AND as a jumbo, and those are two different objects he owns.
NO NUMBER IS RECORDED WHERE HE DID NOT GIVE ONE. Jumbo cards often carry the
same promo number as their standard-size twin, and the owner's standard Greninja
ex promo is 099, but 'often' is not evidence and this file does not hold
inferred numbers any more. Ask him rather than deriving it.

_pidNote: `pid` on a promo or jumbo is its TCGplayer product id, read 22 September 2026 off TCGplayer's own listing: set 'ME: Mega Evolution Promo' for the six promos and 'Jumbo Cards' for the two jumbos, each titled '<name> - <number> (30th Celebration)'. Every _200w.jpg answered 200 image/jpeg before it went in. It is the only picture source these have: TCGdex holds no MEP promos and the binder checklist does not list them. The eight Energy (MEE 009-016) carry one too, from TCGplayer's 'MEE: Mega Evolution Energies' set (713248-713255), read 23 September 2026; each scan was opened and shows the 30th Celebration YOSHIROTTEN foil with the matching type and number.
